clue.text: Kind of screen many demand

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so crosswords use it for many
to demand something is to ask for it

explanation.surface: Lots of people are calling for a particular sort of screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask is a covering that hides or shields the face, a kind of screen.

clue.text: Tea-time's no different in a home

indicators.note: different says the letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea is no different in someone's household.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Notes the balance

definitions.meaning: a series of musical notes in order of pitch

explanation.definitionFit: A scale is both a musical sequence of notes and a weighing device.

clue.text: When there isn't any strong drink it can be very dull

parts.note: spirit is strong alcoholic drink such as whisky or gin
the suffix -less marks the absence of something

explanation.surface: A dry party with no hard liquor can be a real bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking vigour or liveliness, a flat lifeless thing is dull in the extreme.

clue.text: Fenced in holding for, a countryman

indicators.note: holding means containing the following words inside

parts.note: pent means penned or fenced in
as can mean for, in the role of
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rustic kept in an enclosure, apparently on someone's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a farm worker or rustic, a man of the country.

clue.text: Jingle about fish that's staggering

indicators.note: about places the jingle around the fish

parts.note: to ring is to jingle, as bells do
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A catchy jingle about fish that is truly astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' looks like astonishing; here it means lurching about.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling means swaying or tottering, unsteady on one's feet.

clue.text: Transport to school

explanation.surface: Getting children to school.
explanation.definitionFit: A train carries passengers by rail, and to train someone is to school them.

clue.text: Looks over 6 down — makes personal complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: eyes are looks, as in making eyes
a cross-reference to that clue's answer, the railway transport

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at a locomotive and grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'over' puts EYES above the answer to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is a tiredness of the eyes, an ailment of one's own.

clue.text: This party has some dangerous ideas

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political party accused of harbouring risky notions.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a party or faction in a contest or dispute.

clue.text: The sort to challenge the printed word

parts.note: type means sort or kind
to face someone is to confront or challenge them

explanation.surface: The kind of person who would dispute what is written.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is a design of lettering used in printing.

clue.text: No matter what is packed by no matter whom

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning whatever happens, regardless
something packed by anybody at all ends up in somebody's luggage, inside any piece of it

explanation.surface: Whatever the circumstances, it does not matter who does the packing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for regardless or anyhow, used to dismiss other considerations.

clue.text: A capital forward!

parts.note: capital comes from Latin caput, the head, and a head can be the top or chief part

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone onward, as if cheering an excellent advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Going forward means moving to the front, in front of the others.

clue.text: A bloomer from a bovine point of view

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal
an eye is the organ one views from, a point of view

explanation.surface: Something seen as a cow or bull would see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it means a flower: the oxeye daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a white wild flower, and a flower is something that blooms.

clue.text: Put off writing article about falsification and scoffed

indicators.note: about means around, so the article's letters are placed round the lie

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is a falsification of the truth
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: Someone postponed writing a piece about forgery and had a meal instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' is padding with no job in the wordplay; read it as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off is to estrange or repel them, turning them against you.

clue.text: Discriminated against — gets agreed damages

indicators.note: damages says the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A claimant wins settlement money for unfair treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Segregated means kept apart, as by racial separation, a form of discrimination.

clue.text: A quarter support the worker, which is smart

parts.note: E for east is one of the four quarters of the compass
a leg is a support, as for a table
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Someone backs a labourer, and it is called a clever move.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and well dressed, as smart does.

clue.text: They seek answers from a group of underground workers

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex works
miners work below ground

explanation.surface: Questions are put by people from a coal-mining team.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners set questions and look for correct replies.

clue.text: Pitch in to annoy class

indicators.note: in places the pitch inside the word for annoying

parts.note: to grate on someone is to annoy them
an ad, an advertisement, is a sales pitch

explanation.surface: Someone throws a ball in to irritate a class of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch in' looks like a phrase meaning help out; 'Pitch' is the ad, 'in' the container sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To gradate is to sort into grades or steps, which is to class things.

clue.text: Rat running amok — think it could be poison

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: to opine is to think or hold an opinion

explanation.surface: A rat dashing about madly is suspected of being toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade.

clue.text: Exploit a rodent's potential

indicators.note: potential means what these letters could become once reshaped

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Making the most of what a rat or mouse might achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade on something is to take advantage of it for gain.

clue.text: Sewers that are almost completely superfluous

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: needless means wholly unnecessary

explanation.surface: Drains that are nearly entirely unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains; it means things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are the tools that stitch, so they are things that sew.

clue.text: Business associate giving some direction with evident hesitation

parts.note: part means some of a thing
N for north is a compass direction
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A colleague gives partial instructions while plainly umming and erring.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a co-owner or colleague in a firm.

clue.text: French scientist who was behind the French way back

parts.note: past can mean behind, as in time gone by

indicators.note: back means the street word is read in reverse

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A French researcher who lagged behind the French long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RUE into EUR. Louis Pasteur pioneered pasteurisation and vaccines.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist and microbiologist.

clue.text: Listen to subordinate without paying much attention

parts.note: to mind someone is to heed or listen to them
less can mean lower in rank, subordinate

explanation.surface: Advice to heed a junior who is not concentrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless means heedless, done without thought or care.

clue.text: Persuade the trainee to speak slowly

parts.note: to draw someone is to coax or lure them
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: Coaxing a novice into speaking at a slower pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy, drawn-out manner of talking.

clue.text: Prig replacing one on the point

indicators.note: replacing says one letter of the prig is swapped for another word

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-righteous person is put in someone's place, right on the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' takes the place of I (one) in PRIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a pointed tine, as on a fork.

clue.text: Proclaim there's nothing to value

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to rate something is to value it

explanation.surface: Declaring that something is worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak grandly in public, declaiming.

clue.text: Antique silver presented to a ' leading journalist

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an editor, ed, heads a newspaper's staff

explanation.surface: Old silverware given as a gift to a top newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique things are very old, as aged ones are.

clue.text: In the Lake District a river can look great

definitions.text: In the Lake District a river

indicators.note: can look says these letters may appear differently, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Cumbrian stream that can appear magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Greta flows through Keswick in the Lake District, the mountain region of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greta is a river of Cumbria, flowing through Keswick.

clue.text: Plan a surprise attack — tell stories while biding one's time

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
someone biding their time is in wait

explanation.surface: Someone schemes an ambush, lying all the while they wait.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to ambush someone.

clue.text: See in a record certain enlightenment

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
lo is an old word meaning see or look
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Looking at a record brings undoubted illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclosure reveals something, bringing knowledge or enlightenment.

clue.text: Legal document, however it may be regarded

indicators.note: however it is looked at, from either end, it reads the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A legal paper that stays the same whatever view one takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a signed legal instrument, such as one transferring property.
